title: Skybridge: Bounded Staleness for Distributed Caches
problem: Distributed caching requires tradeoffs between consistency and performance; strict consistency limits scalability while eventual consistency allows staleness
motivation: AI systems use distributed caches for model serving and feature caching; bounded staleness provides better consistency guarantees than eventual consistency
method: The system stores frequently-used data across multiple computers. Instead of requiring all machines to always use the newest data (strict consistency—which is slow to coordinate) or allowing them to serve arbitrarily old data (eventual consistency—which is unpredictable), it offers a middle ground: you set a maximum age for how old cached data can get, and the system automatically enforces that limit. This enables quick data access while guaranteeing nothing is older than your specified bound.
key_novelty: The key idea is explicitly and practically controlling data staleness—you set a maximum age that the system enforces for cached data, rather than choosing between always-fresh data (slow) or unpredictably stale data.
contributions: Bounded staleness consistency model for distributed caches
Practical implementation with configurable staleness bounds
Better consistency than eventual consistency with scalability benefits
limitations: Title-only paper; performance/consistency tradeoffs not quantified; applicability to different cache workloads unclear
